title: Rheumatologist Perceptions of Advanced Therapies in Moderate-to-Severe Rheumatoid Arthritis
intro: Thank you for participating. This survey takes approximately 15 minutes. Your responses are confidential and reported only in aggregate.

loops.note: Repeat Q2-Q3 for each therapy selected at Q1, in the order listed at Q1, up to the first 3 selected. Pipe the current therapy name into each question.

computed.label: COST/ACCESS WEIGHT
computed.note: Points allocated to 'Cost and access' (row r5) at Q6.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes your primary professional role?

options.label: I do not treat patients with rheumatoid arthritis

rules.reason: Does not treat rheumatoid arthritis patients.

questions.text: How many years have you been treating patients with rheumatoid arthritis?
questions.instruction: Enter a whole number between 0 and 50.

questions.text: Which of the following best describes your primary practice setting?
Which of the following advanced therapies do you currently prescribe for moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis?

rules.reason: Does not prescribe any advanced RA therapy.

questions.text: How satisfied are you with {LOOP} for your moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis patients?
Approximately what percentage of your advanced-therapy RA patients currently receive {LOOP}?
questions.instruction: Enter a whole number between 0 and 100.

questions.text: Which one advanced therapy would you call your first choice for a biologic- and JAK-naive patient with moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis?
How likely are you to continue prescribing {Q4} at your current rate over the next 12 months?
questions.instruction: 0 = Not at all likely, 10 = Extremely likely

piping.note: Insert the therapy selected at Q4 into the question text.

questions.text: Allocate 100 points across the following factors according to how much each drives your choice of advanced therapy in moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis.
questions.instruction: Enter a whole number in every row. Points must sum to exactly 100.

questions.text: You allocated 40 or more points to cost and access. Which access hurdle affects your prescribing most?
What single change would most improve outcomes for your moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis patients?
How likely are you to recommend advanced therapy to a colleague treating moderate-to-severe rheumatoid arthritis?
questions.instruction: 0 = Not at all likely, 10 = Extremely likely
